identity.name: NEUROGLYPHS Agent
identity.role: Indie game developer working on a glyph-based generative kaleidoscope explorer
identity.stack: Zero-build vanilla JS ESM + Three.js r160 via CDN import map (no bundler, no dependencies)

concept.summary: Endless generative kaleidoscope explorer. Infinite 3D worlds made entirely of glyphs, formulas and light. Seed = world. Music = heartbeat. No goal, no death. Collected "things" fold into the seed and shape the next world. Every world has exactly ONE rectangular exit with a shaped hole.
concept.deprecated: Concept v1 (collecting tokens into a bounded context window, inference events, synapses, neural-network layers, src/systems, src/ui, src/data) is DEAD. Surviving v1 wording is stale text to delete, never a requirement.

principle.description: All visuals are glyphs (characters, formulas, symbols) rendered in 3D. No solid meshes, no image textures, no character models.
principle.invariant: Any new visual element must be a glyph or a glyph-like symbol.

principle.description: World generation is seeded. Same seed produces the same world.
principle.invariant: Never use Math.random() for world gen; always use the rng from src/core/seed.js (mulberry32 lives in src/core/rng.js).

principle.description: The glyph world must stay at 60fps with 5k+ glyphs on integrated GPU.
principle.invariant: Prefer points, instanced or sprite rendering. Avoid per-glyph draw calls beyond ~1000.

principle.description: The player never dies and can never lose. The reward is the place itself.
principle.invariant: No health, no punishing timers, no game-over path. The player can always change world or music.

principle.description: Music is the heartbeat: pulsation, colour and motion react to beat, frequency and mood.
principle.invariant: Reactivity must degrade gracefully to a built-in generator when no audio file is loaded.

principle.description: Each world has exactly one exit: a rectangular frame with a shaped hole.
principle.invariant: The exit is always present, always rectangular, always reachable, visually distinct from the structure.

module.description: Seeded randomness, seed codec, glyph material

file.role: mulberry32 seeded PRNG plus string-to-uint32 hash
Seed codec: 8 world fields bit-packed into a base36 code. encodeSeed, decodeSeed, randomSeed, validateSeed, FIELDS, GROUP_MAX
buildGlyphAtlas: canvas texture atlas from the glyph set

module.description: World generation from a decoded seed

file.role: Pure layout functions per structure type, returning typed arrays, no Three.js
generateWorld, disposeWorld, getExitPosition: structure plus particles plus fog plus exit portal
Import map for Three.js r160, canvas host, DOM HUD
Boot: read the seed URL param, build the world, camera, controls, render loop
Static file server for npm run dev
Seed round-trip on 200 random parameter sets, prints SEED_OK

invariants.invariant: World generation must use the seeded RNG, never Math.random()
All visuals are glyph-based (or shader effects on glyph geometry)
One world = one seed, same seed = same world
No player death, no fail state
Music drives all pulsation and reactivity
The exit is always rectangular and always findable
Same seed plus same collected things = same next world
No text inside the world, textual feedback belongs to the DOM HUD
Glyph textures must be disposed when rebuilt to avoid GPU memory leaks

verification.check: npm test prints DETERMINISM_OK and SEED_OK, plus WORLD_OK from T03 on
npm run dev, open the printed URL, confirm the glyph world renders and the camera responds with no console errors
Reloading the same seed gives an identical world, a different seed gives a visibly different one
Exactly one rectangular exit exists and is reachable
FPS stays at or above 55 at default world size (5000+ glyphs)

notes.note: Node cannot import three because the import map is browser-only. Keep pure math in exported functions and test those.
No bundler and no dependencies: npm run build is a deliberate no-op.
